newsitem.title: USA: Orange County, Merrill Lynch trial set for 1998.
newsitem.headline: Orange County, Merrill Lynch trial set for 1998.

text.p: A judge Monday set a September 1998 trial date for the $2-billion-plus lawsuit by Orange County, California, against brokerage giant Merrill Lynch & Co.
The county filed the bankruptcy-related lawsuit against Merrill Lynch in January 1995, alleging the firm sold it risky securities in violation of state law.
Merrill Lynch has denied any wrongdoing and has asserted the losses were the result of the county's "ill-advised" decision to declare bankruptcy.
At a court hearing in Santa Ana late Monday, U.S. District Judge Gary Taylor told the county and Merrill Lynch that the case would go to trial on Sept. 15, 1998.
Merrill Lynch had argued that it needed more than one year to prepare its defence because of the complexity of the case. The county sought less time to prepare for trial.
"We will prepare for trial and expect to be ready by the date set by the judge," Merrill Lynch spokesman Timothy Gilles said following the hearing.
County attorneys said the 1998 trial date was fair. "We'd like it to be a little sooner, but that's the judge's job," county attorney Michael Hennigan said.
Orange County filed for protection under Chapter 9 of the federal Bankruptcy Code on Dec.6, 1994 after sustaining investment losses of more than $1.6 billion.
The county emerged from bankruptcy last June.
The county has sued several firms to recover the funds it lost, including Merrill Lynch, credit rating agency Standard & Poor's Corp. and brokerage firm Morgan Stanley & Co.
